summary: The note explains that the term 'New Journalism' was given its current meaning by Tom Wolfe. Wolfe used it for a 1973 collection of journalism articles he published under the title The New Journalism. The collection included works by several writers, including Truman Capote, Hunter S. Thompson, Norman Mailer, Joan Didion, Terry Southern, Robert Christgau, and Gay Talese.
one_line: Overview of the term 'New Journalism', codified by Tom Wolfe in his 1973 anthology of journalism articles.
key_facts: The term 'New Journalism' was codified with its current meaning by Tom Wolfe.
Tom Wolfe published a collection of journalism articles titled The New Journalism in 1973.
The 1973 collection The New Journalism included works by Tom Wolfe himself.
The 1973 collection The New Journalism included works by Truman Capote.
The 1973 collection The New Journalism included works by Hunter S. Thompson.
The 1973 collection The New Journalism included works by Norman Mailer.
The 1973 collection The New Journalism included works by Joan Didion.
The 1973 collection The New Journalism included works by Terry Southern.
The 1973 collection The New Journalism included works by Robert Christgau.
The 1973 collection The New Journalism included works by Gay Talese.
The 1973 collection The New Journalism also included works by other writers beyond those named in the note.
